sources.title: Livestock mobility in sub-Saharan Africa: A critical review
sources.accessed: Primary open-access article, introduction and mobility sections read via publisher
sources.used_for: Separate daily grazing orbits around bases from travel between bases; distinguish water, forage and social access. No universal movement distance, herd-size, institution or nomad-from-biome rule imported.

sources.title: The Logistics of the Roman Army at War (264 BC–AD 235)
sources.accessed: Author/publisher bibliographic description and scope; full book not read
sources.used_for: Historical framing: food needs, storage, sources and supply lines must be distinguished from mere reach. No historical ration, capacity or troop-number coefficients claimed from this source.

sources.title: Manual of the prevention of post-harvest grain losses — The fundamentals of storage
sources.used_for: Stored grain deteriorates through moisture, biological activity and pests; scenario decay is explicit. The chosen 5% annual stored-energy decay is an uncalibrated sensitivity assumption, not a universal ancient loss rate.

sources.authors: Ford, L. R., Jr.; Fulkerson, D. R.
sources.title: Constructing Maximal Dynamic Flows from Static Flows
sources.used_for: Separate transit times and capacities in time-indexed material accounting. Present implementation uses fixed collection trees and repeating inventory ledgers, not a reproduction of the paper's theorem or free trade optimization.

inference: All staffing, rations, collection rates, freight capacities, stores, travel budgets, herd demand and water filters are declared scenarios. No validation of actual control, settlements, pastoral institutions or political systems is inferred from these sources.
